title: 〜を機に / 〜を機として
romaji: wo ki ni / wo ki to shite
meaning: taking … as an opportunity; on the occasion of …; … became the trigger for
simpleExplanation: 〜を機に names an event that became a turning point: because that event happened, the speaker took a new action or something new began. 機 (き) means "chance, occasion". The event itself is not the cause; it is the moment the speaker used to make a change.
whenUsed: Formal but very common: announcements, business writing, life-event stories (結婚・退職・引っ越し・出産), and news about policy changes. 〜を機として is a stiffer written variant. In casual speech 〜をきっかけに is more usual.
formation: N + を機として (more formal, written)
Vた / Vる + の + を機に  (退職したのを機に)
Typical nouns: 結婚・出産・退職・卒業・転勤・事故・事件・受賞

steps.en: the event is treated as a turning point

steps.ja: 結婚を機に、郊外へ引っ越した

examples.ja: 結婚を機に、都心から郊外へ引っ越した。
examples.reading: けっこんをきに、としんからこうがいへひっこした。
examples.en: Taking marriage as the occasion, we moved from the city center to the suburbs.
examples.note: Marriage is the occasion; moving house is the new action the couple decided on.

examples.ja: 退職を機に、長年の夢だった世界一周の旅に出た。
examples.reading: たいしょくをきに、ながねんのゆめだったせかいいっしゅうのたびにでた。
examples.en: On retiring, I set out on the round-the-world trip that had long been my dream.
examples.note: 退職 + を機に + a long-held plan is a very common life-story pattern.

examples.ja: この事故を機として、安全基準が見直された。
examples.reading: このじこをきとして、あんぜんきじゅんがみなおされた。
examples.en: Taking this accident as a trigger, the safety standards were reviewed.
examples.note: を機として is the formal written version, typical of official reports about reforms.

examples.ja: 子供が生まれたのを機に、たばこをやめた。
examples.reading: こどもがうまれたのをきに、たばこをやめた。
examples.en: When my child was born, I took the opportunity to quit smoking.
examples.note: A clause can be used with の + を機に.

examples.ja: 創立五十周年を機に、会社は新しいロゴを発表した。
examples.reading: そうりつごじっしゅうねんをきに、かいしゃはあたらしいロゴをはっぴょうした。
examples.en: On the occasion of its fiftieth anniversary, the company unveiled a new logo.
examples.note: Anniversaries and milestones are natural occasions for を機に.

similarGrammar.difference: Same idea, but more casual and everyday. を機に sounds more formal and is preferred in writing.
The stiffest of the three; typical of newspapers and official documents. Often used for large social changes rather than personal life events.
Marks a dividing line after which things are different. を境に describes a change that happened; を機に describes an action someone chose to take.

commonMistakes.wrong: 結婚を機に、幸せになった。
commonMistakes.right: 結婚を機に、家を買った。
commonMistakes.why: The main clause should be a deliberate new action or a clear new start, not a vague result or feeling.

commonMistakes.wrong: 雨が降ったのを機に、試合が中止になった。
commonMistakes.right: 雨が降ったので、試合が中止になった。
commonMistakes.why: を機に is not a cause. A cancellation forced by rain is a plain cause-and-effect, so use ので / ため.

commonMistakes.wrong: 退職を機会に、旅に出た。
commonMistakes.why: The grammar pattern uses 機 alone. 機会 is a normal noun ("opportunity") and does not form this construction.

usageNotes: Set phrases: これを機に ("taking this as an opportunity") and 〜を機に〜を始める / やめる / 見直す.
The event is usually something significant and positive or neutral (a milestone), though accidents can trigger reforms (事故を機として).
In speeches you will hear 本日の〜を機に、〜てまいります, a polite way to announce a new commitment.
jlptTips: In 文法形式の判断, when the sentence has a life event noun (結婚・退職・出産) followed by a deliberate new action, choose を機に.
Common distractors: を境に, にかけて, をもって. Ask whether the person actively started something (を機に) or whether things simply changed after a point (を境に).
In 並べ替え, keep the chunk を機に right after the event noun; the new action comes last.
